newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn cuts standard income tax rate to 26 pct.
newsitem.headline: Quinn cuts standard income tax rate to 26 pct.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said he was cutting the standard income tax rate to 26 percent from 27 percent, the first such cut in five years.
Quinn also told the Irish parliament in his budget speech that the employee PRSI (pay-related social insurance) for Class A and Class H contributors would be reduced by one percentage point.
"This reduction in social insurance contribution will assist over 70 percent of PRSI contributors, including those outside the income tax net," Quinn said.
The standard income tax band is being widened to 500 pounds for single persons to 9,900 pounds and for married couples to 19,800 pounds, he said.

"But taken together, this is the biggest tax reduction package in the history of the state," Quinn said. "It will benefit the majority of the 1.3 million people currently at work and it has an annual full year value of over 490 million pounds."

Quinn said the general income tax exemption limits below which no income tax is paid, will be raised by 100 pounds to 4,000 pounds per year for single persons and by 200 pounds to 8,000 pounds for married couples.
"This will remove around 10,000 persons who would otherwise be in the tax net," Quinn said.
